listen: Good morning. This is The Daily Brief for Thursday, November 19. Here is what matters today. Our lead story is Anthropic. The company has priced its initial public offering at 83 dollars a share. NPR says the offering raised a record 81.3 billion dollars. The five-year-old AI company drew strong demand. That came even as concern grows about a possible AI bubble and swings in tech stocks. For anyone who builds tools with Claude, this is a big moment for the company. Now the front page. President Trump is set to meet Russia's Vladimir Putin and China's Xi Jinping on Thursday. NPR calls it a historic three-way meeting. In Washington, House Democrats voted overwhelmingly to nominate Hakeem Jeffries for speaker. If he wins the job, he would be the first Black lawmaker to hold it. In basketball, the Houston Rockets beat the Indiana Pacers 119 to 104. Kevin Durant scored 21 points. Reed Sheppard made six three-pointers. But Houston lost Alperen Sengun to injury. The Rockets visit Denver on Friday. In science, Voyager 1 has reached one light-day from Earth. No other human-made object has traveled that far. Now the sections. In tech, Simon Willison says Google's new Gemini 4 Neon makes an already confusing pricing lineup worse. Anthropic also announced a wider partnership with the General Services Administration to bring Claude to government. In politics, The Lever reports that Trump's pick to lead the FDA was withdrawn after senators reportedly objected to the nominee's views. Congressman Brendan Boyle proposes a tax on private jet purchases to help pay for air safety. In world news, dozens are missing after a boat carrying about 100 migrants sank off Senegal. Russia says the Crimean Bridge was attacked again, and traffic was suspended. Survivors of a deadly landslide in Uganda are seeking justice at the United Nations. In sports, 49ers star Nick Bosa says he is not playing his best after four games without a sack. Christian McCaffrey earned a FedEx honor for his huge game against Dallas. And the UFC released strawweight Virna Jandiroba, who was ranked third. In Atlanta, new Fulton County Commissioner Rohit Malhotra introduced legislation to declare gun violence a public health crisis. The city's pro women's soccer club unveiled plans for a new training facility. MARTA also outlined a station expansion. In architecture, a new BIM platform called Pliera aims to challenge Revit. Rayon version four brings an AI agent to browser-based CAD. And a small Kyoto villa makes use of a very narrow lot. In science and nature, astronomers watched two stars merge in the Andromeda galaxy. El Niño rains brought a vast flowering to Chile's Atacama. And NASA is targeting November 29 for the next cargo launch to the space station. That is the brief. Have a good day.

lead.title: Anthropic IPO raises record $81.3 billion on strong AI demand
lead.note: Anthropic has priced its initial public offering at $83 a share, raising a record $81.3 billion. NPR describes the five-year-old company as an artificial intelligence powerhouse and says the offering met strong demand for AI. The pricing came despite growing concern about a possible AI bubble and volatility in tech stocks. For this reader, it matters because the company behind Claude is now moving from private ownership to public markets, after its earlier filing and roadshow. The amount raised is described as a record, which gives a plain sense of how much investor appetite there is for AI right now. Anyone who builds personal tools on Claude may want to follow how the company changes as a public firm, and how markets react in the days ahead.
